instruction: Using catalogue records as observed on 9 September 2026, identify Apache HTTP Server vulnerabilities first published from 1 January 2020 through 31 December 2023 inclusive, using the catalogue publication timestamp rather than the year embedded in the CVE identifier. Include only records whose current applicability configurations contain an Apache HTTP Server CPE match marked vulnerable; a match describing only a non-vulnerable required environment does not qualify. Among these records, retain those for which the NIST CVSS v3.1 base vector added in the earliest NIST Initial Analysis event differs from the current NIST CVSS v3.1 base vector. Compare the base metric values, ignoring the display prefix, and use NIST assessments only, not CNA or other contributor assessments. A record must have both of these NIST v3.1 assessments to qualify. For each retained record, report its CVE identifier, the base score computed from that initial vector, the current NIST v3.1 base score, and the UTC calendar date of the earliest subsequent NIST analysis-history event that actually changed that base vector. Reference-link edits, CPE changes, and additions by other contributors are not vector revisions. NIST Reanalysis and Modified Analysis events both count if they change the vector. This is a catalogue-history audit, not a present-day risk ranking. Establish the complete product and publication cohort, distinguish vulnerable product matches from environment-only matches, then use the resulting CVE identities to retrieve their change histories. Separate NIST from other sources, reconstruct the initial and first revised base vectors, and compare the initial vector with the current NIST assessment before deciding inclusion.
output_format: Return only a pipe-separated table with header cve_id|initial_base_score|current_base_score|first_revision_date. Use standard CVE identifiers, decimal base scores and YYYY-MM-DD dates. Sort rows lexicographically by cve_id.
